This case arises out of the complaint filed by the complainant against the accused under section 200

2. The case

It is the case of the complainant is that the complainant is a limited company incorporated under the companies Act.

The object of the complainant company is to render financial assistance and lend money and grant loan on security of the immovable properties, personal security, gold and silver articles, machineries of commercial value etc.
It is further stated that the accused is one of the customer of the complainant company.

The accused and his son, Sri. Kiran Krishnan and Sri.S.Rupesh Kumar S/o M.Sainath jointly on 03.01.2012 availed the two loans from the complainant in Loan Account No.SLA 1081 and Loan Account No.SLA 1082 of Rs.5,00,000/- each.
On the same day they have executed on demand promissory note in favour of the complainant company promising to pay the said amount with interest at the rate of 24% p.a,. for value received.
They have received the loan amount and C.C.NO.17673/2019 executed take Delivery letter, on demand promissory note and acknowledged the receipt of the loan amount.

3. It is further stated that the accused and his wife Smt.Ganga Krishnan and one Sri.S.Rupesh Kumar S/o Sri.M.Sainath on 09.01.2013 jointly availed another loan of Rs.5,00,000/- (Account No.SLA 1124) by executing on demand promissory note, take deliver letter and consideration receipt.
The accused and the other co- borrowers failed to repay the loan amount at the agreed terms.
Under the aforesaid three loan accounts, the accused and other co-borrowers are due to the complainant company a sum of Rs.23,68,703/- as on 31.07.2018.

The accused towards part repayment of the aforesaid loan amount had issued the cheque bearing No.192262 dated:
23.08.2018 for a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- and cheque bearing No.192263 dated: 27.08.2018 for a sum of Rs.7,00,000/-
, both cheques were drawn on the Indian Bank, Chamarajpet Branch, Bangalore, in favour of the complainant.
The complainant had presented the said cheques for encashment through its Banker the Canara Bank, Madhavanagar Branch, Bangalore.
But the said cheques were dishonored on 24.08.2018 and 28.08.2018 with an endorsements "Funds Insufficient" in the account of the accused.
The complainant received endorsements on 29.08.2018.

Thereafter the complainant got issued a legal notice to the accused on 01.09.2018 through its counsel by RPAD calling upon him to pay the cheque amount within 15 days from the C.C.NO.17673/2019 date of receipt of the said notice.
The said notice was received by the accused and on 08.09.2018 issued an untenable reply through his advocate.
But the accused has failed to repay the cheques amount.
As such, the accused has committed an offence punishable under section 138 of N.I.Act.
Hence, the present complaint came to be filed before this court on 17.10.2018.
